DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 24 s. 2022 APR 18 2022 Hon. XENIA JANE O. ECHEMINADA Sangguniang Bayan Member Municipality of Impasugong Bukidnon Poblacion, Impasugong Bukidnon, xenia_echeminada@yahoo.com Dear SB Member Echeminada. This refers to your letter dated 04 February 2022 requesting for this Department's legal opinion on the following issues: 1. Whether or not Barangay Workers like Barangay Health Workers (BHWs), Barangay Nutrition Scholars (BNS), and Barangay Day Care Workers (BDCWs) are within the purview of Barangay Officials provided in the Local Government Code of 1991. 2. Whether or not the BHWs be issued appointment by the Punong Barangay in the light of the RA 7883 definition (paragraph (a) Section 5) of "Barangay Health Workers refers to a person who voluntarily renders primary health care services in the Community." And the IRR, defines "Voluntary Services" (paragraph (1) Section 5, Rule I) refers to health and health-related activities rendered by a BHW on his/her own free will, responsive to the needs of the community, and for which he/she has no certificate at appointment and is not given any renumeration or salary." (underscoring supplied). 3. There might be some amendments to RA 7883 or there is a new law pertaining to the welfare of Barangay workers that this Sanggunian is not aware of, hence this request for clarification. We respectfully submit that Barangay Day Care Workers are barangay officials duly appointed pursuant to a valid local ordinance. Meanwhile, BHWs and BNSs may be either voluntary personnel or barangay officials. Barangay Health Worker Republic Act No. 7883 (RA 7883) and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) remains to be the main law governing BHWs. RA 7883, however, states that the law and its IRR only cover registered and accredited BHWs who render voluntary service, to wit: Rule I. Section 3. Coverage. These Rules and Regulations shall cover all registered or accredited BHWs nationwide trained in Primary Health Care by either a government or non- "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

government organization (NGO) whose primary health care training programs have been duly accredited to function as such by the Department of Health (DOH) and who voluntarily render primary health care services in their own communities, barangay health stations and rural health units; provided that they are not receiving salaries from any government or institution. In DILG Opinion No. 42, series of 2000, this Department stated that voluntary undertaking does not constitute service pursuant to a public service: "Being a mere voluntary undertaking, services as barangay health workers rendered under the aforesaid law cannot be considered as services rendered pursuant to a public office since the latter connotes the nature of being continuous or which involves the idea of tenure, duration or continuance (63 Am. St. Rep. 189)." As you have correctly manifested, BHWs covered by RA 7883 render voluntary service on their own free will, and without any remuneration or certificate of appointment. BHWs who fall under the definition above are not barangay officials, and merely act as voluntary personnel. RA 7883 and its IRR, however, does not prohibit or prevent a barangay from creating the position of "barangay health worker or official" provided the same is done through an ordinance. Under Republic Act No. 7160, or the Local Government Code (LGC), the Sangguniang Barangay is authorized to create positions as it may deem necessary to carry out the purposes of the barangay government in accordance with the needs of public service, subject to the budgetary limitations prescribed by the LGC, and the Department of Budget and Management. 1 A barangay is therefore empowered to create the position of BHW should it's Sanggunian deem the same necessary. Such BHW is a barangay official, and requires a certificate of appointment from the barangay. BHWs under RA 7883 are entitled to hazard allowance; subsistence allowance; training, education and career enrichment programs; second grade Civil Service Eligibility, free legal service, and preferential access to loans. Meanwhile, BHWs who are appointed by the barangay and/or receive salary on an ordinary basis are entitled to the benefits under the ordinance creating the position. In DILG Opinion No. 42, series of 2000, this Department affirmed the difference between a voluntary and an appointed BHW: . Precisely, barangay health workers mobilized under RA 7883 do not need any appointment or designation as such. They need only to be accredited by their respective local health boards in accordance with the guidelines promulgated by the Department of Health (2nd par., Sec. 3, Ibid).. . However, if an elective or appointive official works as a barangay health worker by virtue of an appointment to a duly created office by the sangguniang barangay for the aforesaid position, we believe that the prohibition found in Section 94 of RA 7160 would apply except perhaps for any appointive official who is allowed by law or the primary functions of his office to be appointed as barangay health worker.. To summarize, a BHW duly appointed by the barangay pursuant to an ordinance creating such position is considered as a barangay official. Such BHW shall require a certificate of appointment prior to his/her undertaking. Meanwhile, a registered and accredited BHW who renders voluntary services in accordance RA 7883 and its IRR does not require the aforesaid certificate of appointment. Barangay Nutrition Scholar As per Presidential Decree No. 1569, BNSs are barangay-based volunteer workers responsible for delivering nutrition services and other related activities to the barangay.2 As a voluntary undertaking, qualified voluntary BNS do not serve as barangay officials. Similar to BHWs, a barangay is not precluded from establishing the position of BNS through a valid ordinance, and appointing the personnel by the issuance of a certificate of appointment. Barangay Day Care Worker Lastly, we respectfully submit that this Department has confirmed that BDCWs are barangay officials in a Letter dated 16 April 2020 issued by the Undersecretary for Plans, Public Affairs, and Communications to the Department of Social Welfare and Development. We cite the pertinent portion of the Letter as follows: "Barangay Day Care Workers Barangay Day Care Workers belong to those positions Other than the mandatory barangay officials which may be created h the barangay and may be compensated in the form of salary or honorarium at the discretion of the barangay government concerned. Thus, Barangay Day Care Workers are appointed by the barangay when a position for such is created by the unit.. BDCWs are therefore barangay officials which require the issuance of a certificate of appointment prior to the assumption of office. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to addressed your concerns. Thank you. Y AUTHORITY OF THE S CRETARY: M B.
